If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

Notice that only the $z$-component of $F=⟨0,\,0,\,{x}^{2}-yz⟩$ is non-zero. Since the lateral sides of $S$ are parallel to the $z$-axis, the flux of $F$ through $S$ will be non-zero only at the top and bottom sides. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14275251/assets/fdaad0039f4b7fea5c6e301f4cc3b89687f5f4081e3bd87f8ce31daacda2744b.png)

 

Let's consider the flux of $F$ through these two sides.

- Let ${S}_{1}$ denote the top surface. On this surface, we have $z=2$ for $0\le x\le 3$ and $0\le y\le 2.$ The outward-pointing unit normal vector to ${S}_{1}$ is

$$
{n}_{1}=⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩.
$$

Using the fact that $z=2$ on ${S}_{1},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot {n}_{1} & =⟨0,\,0,\,{x}^{2}-yz⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,{x}^{2}-2y⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & ={x}^{2}-2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across ${S}_{1}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot {n}_{1}\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}{x}^{2}-2y\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}-2y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}-2y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-2xy]}_{x=0}^{x=3}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}9-6y\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[9y-3{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

- Let ${S}_{2}$ denote the bottom surface. On this surface, we have $z=0$ for $0\le x\le 3$ and $0\le y\le 2.$ The outward-pointing unit normal vector to ${S}_{2}$ is

$$
{n}_{2}=⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩.
$$

Using the fact that $z=0$ on ${S}_{2},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot {n}_{2} & =⟨0,\,0,\,{x}^{2}-yz⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,{x}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\  & =-{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across ${S}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot {n}_{2}\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}-{x}^{2}\,\text{d}S \\  & =-{∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{2}9\,\text{d}y \\  & =-9[y]_{0}^{2} \\  & =-18.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & =6+(-18) \\  & =-12.\end{aligned}
$$
